description: Declared rules that assign required evidence categories to plan obligations. A rule applies to an obligation when every condition it states holds (conditions: rules = verification rule ids from verification-rules.json, gates, documents, requirements = selector grammar of Model.matches, titlePattern = .NET regex over the requirement title, obligationKinds, obligations = exact baseline obligation ids, freshnessPolicies = the requirement's plan policy); within one condition any listed value matches. Every applicable rule contributes its category; the union is the obligation's required set. An obligation no rule reaches is reported 'unclassified' missing coverage, never assigned a default. Each rule cites the declared requirement data it rests on (source), so a reviewer can check it without reading code.

categories.definition: Deterministic tests of one component in isolation (F# unit and property tests, illegal-transition and forged-history variants); no browser, provider or network.

Tests across a boundary between components or systems: producer/consumer contract tests, recorded-response provider contract tests, storage golden replay, dependency compatibility smoke, catalog verification.
The application exercised in a real browser engine (WebKit/Chromium via Percepta or Playwright), offline-fixture or deployed, including printed and rendered output.
Real requests against the authorized live provider (the GitHub test repository) in the candidate's own run, with independent re-reads; mocked or recorded responses never count.
Evidence that a security property holds: credential handling, least privilege, secret non-disclosure in logs, URLs, screenshots and artifacts.
Accessibility verification: automated accessibility report (axe), keyboard-only and focus checks, reduced motion, screen-reader semantics.
Evidence produced by a party independent of the implementing agent: an independent reviewer's record, or an acceptance job the implementer does not author, bound to the reviewed or deployed SHA.

rules.source: verification-rules.json VR-UI method: "Percepta semantic contract verification of populated states at the deployed exact SHA; WebKit at iPad portrait/landscape, desktop and mobile"
verification-rules.json VR-UI method: "axe accessibility; keyboard and reduced-motion checks"; evidence: "accessibility report"
verification-rules.json VR-DOMAIN method: "F# unit and property tests including illegal-transition and forged-history variants"
verification-rules.json VR-INTERFACE method: "producer/consumer contract tests at the interface-manifest SHA"
verification-rules.json VR-STORAGE method: "three identities match; golden replay of five scenarios; 90 negative fixtures refused"

verification-rules.json VR-PERSISTENCE (gate G6) method: "live create/read/write/reload/conflict/rejected-token against the test repository with independent SHA re-reads"; freshness: "live evidence from this run only"

verification-rules.json VR-PERSISTENCE method: "four verification levels (PF-011)" and "fakes only from recorded responses" (the provider-conformance level, PF-011-O3: shared contract tests against fixture and GitHub adapters)
verification-rules.json VR-DEPENDENCIES method: "lock compared with installed and loaded artifacts; set qualification; compatibility smoke"
verification-rules.json VR-DEFECT-CLASS (gate G7) method: "independent approval, SHA-bound proof"; owner: "independent reviewer + Dokimos"
verification-rules.json VR-DECISIONS (gate G7) owner: "independent architecture review"
verification-rules.json VR-REPORT method: "report fidelity against projections; print rendering"; evidence: "rendered report artifact at the deployed SHA"
verification-rules.json VR-DEPLOYMENT (gate G9) owner: "Dokimos (deployed acceptance)"; method: "successful acceptance job on the same SHA"
verification-rules.json VR-CATALOG method: "catalog verification plus application load after Connect"

baseline requirement titles that name security or credentials (at aab8f80: AR-014 "Secure capability isolation", PF-015 "Credentials and security"); no verification rule declares a security method, so the title is the declared data used

notCategorized.reason: the ledger row is the carrier of claims, not evidence of an obligation
requirements preservation proves the derivation, not the implementation of an obligation
process records (Praxis work items, checkpoints) match none of the seven categories; an obligation reached only by VR-PROCESS is reported unclassified
